title: fix: honor explicit chat limits and tool settings
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Honor either caller token limit before model defaults. Preserve existing max_tokens precedence when both limits are explicit; handle nullable aliases correctly.
- Forward explicit parallel_tool_calls without injecting true into every request. Keep intentional sampling restrictions and deprecated thinking-alias removal from #14585 and #12029.
- Pin merged [gateway #12](https://github.com/pollinations/gateway/pull/12), commit 639928b0af4682e675b0cf0209b79694c01ea330, for Azure parallel tools, generic top_k and Claude effort/JSON schema. Its tree matches the live-tested branch exactly.
- Verification: 227 focused tests, Gen typecheck, Biome and MCP tests pass; 590 limit checks across all 118 routes preserve defaults. Sixteen live probes through local Gen + gateway code reach real providers, covering Azure single/parallel/streaming tools, Claude 32-token output/schema/effort, nullable limits and Fireworks/DeepInfra top_k. Unsupported OVH top_k and invalid Claude inputs return provider 400s. These are not public auth/billing end-to-end tests. Full Enter/Gen CI passed before the pin-only update.
- Addresses forwarding bugs found while reviewing #14599. Parameter metadata remains separate. No production deployment or credential changes.

gist.headline: The knobs now reach the hive
gist.blurb: Chat requests can finally keep their carefully chosen limits and tool settings all the way to the model. Polli checked the wiring; a few parameters had been taking scenic routes.
gist.summary: Fixed Gen chat parameter forwarding so explicit caller token limits take precedence over model defaults, explicit parallel_tool_calls is forwarded without forcing true, and the gateway is pinned to commit 639928b0 for Azure parallel tools, generic top_k, and Claude effort/JSON-schema support.
gist.impact: Developers can now reliably use nullable token-limit aliases, parallel or single tool calls, top_k where supported, and Claude output/schema/effort settings without defaults silently changing an explicit request.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-workshop control panel represents chat request settings reaching their intended model routes: labeled token gauges, a tool-call switch left deliberately in its chosen position, and several gentle cables leading to small Azure, Claude, and generic model terminals. Polli, wearing a tiny electrician tool belt, carefully reconnects the wires while code-plants grow around the terminals; the monitor robot can inspect the now-correct settings.
